Rather, turning to Job, "thou that tearest thyself in anger" (<reference osisRef="Job.5.2">Job 5:2</reference>).<div eID="gen7055" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7056" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be forsaken?--</hi>become desolate. He alludes here to Job's words as to the "rock," crumbling away (<reference osisRef="Job.14.18">Job 14:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.14.19">19</reference>); but in a different application. He says bitterly "for thee." Wert thou not punished as thou art, and as thou art unwilling to bear, the eternal order of the universe would be disturbed and the earth become desolate through unavenged wickedness [Umbreit]. Bildad takes it for granted Job is a great sinner (<reference osisRef="Job.8.3-Job.8.6">Job 8:3-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.24.5">Is 24:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.24.6">6</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4830"/><div sID="gen7059" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4830"/><hi type="bold">6. candle--</hi>the lamp which in the East is usually fastened to the ceiling. To put out the lamp was an image of utter desolation. <div eID="gen7059" type="x-p"/>

The Hebrew expresses, "to stride slowly and solemnly." The godless has a fearful death for long before his eyes, and is at last taken by it. Alluding to Job's case. The King of terrors, not like the heathen Pluto, the tabled ruler of the dead, but Death, with all its terrors to the ungodly, personified. <div eID="gen7073" type="x-p"/>
